analyze-locale-dropdown-info: Locale for the translated species common names in the output
computing-settings-batchsize-number-info: Number of samples processed simultaneously. Leave this value at its default unless you know what you're doing.
computing-settings-producers-number-info: Number of producer processes feeding the inference queue. Leave this value at its default unless you know what you're doing.
computing-settings-workers-auto-checkbox: Starts as many worker processes as fit into the available memory, at most one per CPU core. Uncheck to set the number yourself.
computing-settings-workers-number-info: Number of worker processes used for inference. Each worker loads its own copy of the model, so more workers need more memory.
embedding-settings-audio-speed-slider-in: Negative values slow down, positive values speed up. The audio speed modification will be stored in the database.
embedding-settings-overlap-slider-info: Adjust the overlap between the samples to extract embeddings from.
embeddings-db-already-exists-info: Database already exists, using audio speed and bandpass filter options from database settings.
embeddings-db-dir-validation-message: Please select a directory for the database
embeddings-db-name-validation-message: Please specify a name for the database
embeddings-search-audio-root-validation-: Please select the audio root directory
embeddings-search-crop-mode-radio-info: Adjust how to crop the query sample if it is longer than the model input.
embeddings-search-crop-overlap-number-in: Adjust the overlap of the query sample.
embeddings-search-db-selection-error: Couldn't find a database, make sure to select the directory containing the database.
embeddings-search-db-validation-message: Please select a database to search in
embeddings-search-max-samples-number-lab: Maximum number of samples to search for
embeddings-search-max-samples-validation: Please specify the maximum number of samples to search for
embeddings-search-tab-info-text:
Search an embeddings database created in the Embeddings tab to find sounds that are similar to a query sample.

Select the embeddings database and the audio root it was built from, then choose a query clip and tune the search options such as the number of results.

Run the search to browse the closest matches. The results can help you find additional examples of a target species, for instance to build a training dataset.
embeddings-tab-dp-path-textbox-info: It is recommended to select an empty directory when creating a new database.
embeddings-tab-file-output-directory-tex: If not selected, file output will be omitted
embeddings-tab-info-text:
Create an embeddings database from a directory of audio files. The embeddings capture the acoustic content of your recordings and can later be queried in the Search tab.

Select the source audio directory and the location for the embeddings database. Adjust the settings if needed, for example the audio options or overlap.

Start the process to generate the database, which can then be searched for sounds similar to a query sample.
eval-tab-accuracy-checkbox-info: Accuracy is the share of correct predictions. Since most windows contain no call, true negatives dominate and accuracy stays misleadingly high — so it is off by default.
eval-tab-ap-checkbox-info: Summarizes precision over all recall levels. Independent of the threshold.
eval-tab-auroc-checkbox-info: The probability that a random window with the class scores higher than a random window without it. Independent of the threshold.
eval-tab-averaging-radio-info: How the per-class scores are combined into the overall row. Classes without annotations are left out.
eval-tab-class-mapping-info: A JSON file that renames predicted classes to the names used in your annotations, for example "Eurasian Chaffinch": "Common Chaffinch". Download the template to start one.
eval-tab-classwise-checkbox-info: Draw the plots for each selected class instead of the overall scores.
eval-tab-column-class-info: The class names, written the same way in both directories.
eval-tab-column-confidence-info: The confidence of the prediction, from 0 to 1.
eval-tab-column-duration-info: Column with the length of the recording in seconds.
eval-tab-column-recording-info: Column with the audio file name. Leave empty to pair tables by their file names.
eval-tab-column-time-info: Seconds from the start of the recording.
eval-tab-error-bad-mapping: The class mapping file cannot be used. It must be a JSON object that maps predicted class names to annotation class names; see the template.
eval-tab-error-decimal-comma: Numbers need a decimal point, not a comma.
eval-tab-error-duplicate-annotation-reco: Two annotation tables belong to recordings named "{recording}" ({places}). Tables are paired by recording name, so the names must be unique: select the directories of one site or recorder at a time.
eval-tab-error-duplicate-prediction-reco: Two prediction tables belong to recordings named "{recording}" ({places}). Tables are paired by recording name, so the names must be unique: select the directories of one site or recorder at a time.
eval-tab-error-min-overlap: The minimum overlap must be more than 0 s and at most the window length.
eval-tab-error-missing-annotation-column: The annotation tables have no column "{column}". Choose the column for "{field}" under "Annotation columns". Columns found: {available}
eval-tab-error-missing-prediction-column: The prediction tables have no column "{column}". Choose the column for "{field}" under "Prediction columns". Columns found: {available}
eval-tab-error-no-class-selected: The tables contain no classes to evaluate.
eval-tab-error-no-header: The files seem to have no header row: their first line holds values, not column names.
eval-tab-error-no-valid-recording-durati: Enter the recording duration in seconds, at least the window length, or leave it empty.
eval-tab-error-not-a-number: {file}, row {row}: "{value}" in the column "{column}" is not a number.
eval-tab-error-nothing-paired: None of the annotation tables could be paired with a prediction table, so there is nothing to compare.
eval-tab-error-plot-unavailable: This plot could not be drawn for the current results.
eval-tab-error-plotting-metrics-all-thre: Error plotting metrics for all thresholds
eval-tab-error-reading-tables: The tables could not be read
eval-tab-error-select-folders: Select an annotation directory and a prediction directory first.
eval-tab-error-window-length: Enter a window length in seconds, e.g. 3 for BirdNET or 5 for Perch.
eval-tab-f1-score-checkbox-info: The harmonic mean of precision and recall.
eval-tab-info-text:
Compare the predictions of BirdNET or a custom classifier with your annotations to see how well it works on your recordings and which confidence threshold suits them.

1. **Annotations:** select a directory with one selection table (.txt, e.g. from Raven) per recording, named after the audio file: site1_0530.wav → site1_0530.txt or site1_0530.Table.1.selections.txt. Annotate every call of the classes you evaluate; a recording without calls is a table without rows.
2. **Predictions:** select the output directory of a batch analysis of the same recordings (Raven selection tables or CSV files). To evaluate low thresholds and for AP and AUROC, analyze with a low minimum confidence such as 0.05.
3. Check the summary that appears below the directories: it shows how many recordings and classes could be paired and what to change if names differ.

Each recording is cut into windows of the window length (3 s for BirdNET, 5 s for Perch), and each window is scored once per class, so the scores count windows, not calls.
eval-tab-min-overlap-number-info: How many seconds an annotation or prediction must overlap a window to count for it.
eval-tab-note-annotation-only: Recordings with annotations but no prediction table; all their annotations count as missed ({n}): {names}
eval-tab-note-empty-classes: Selected classes without annotations in the evaluated recordings, shown as n/a and left out of the overall row ({n}): {names}
eval-tab-note-plot-limit: The per-class plots show the {limit} classes with the most annotated windows.
eval-tab-note-threshold-below-scores: The predictions contain no confidence below {min_conf}, so any lower threshold gives the same results as {min_conf}.
eval-tab-note-truncated-scores: AUROC and AP rank all windows by confidence, but the predictions only contain confidences of {min_conf} and above; all other windows count as 0. Compare these values only between analyses with the same minimum confidence, or analyze with a minimum confidence of 0.05.
eval-tab-note-unmatched-dropped: Recordings with predictions but no annotation table, not scored ({n}): {names}
eval-tab-note-unmatched-empty: Recordings with predictions but no annotation table, scored as recordings without calls ({n}): {names}
eval-tab-note-unselected-detections: The predictions also contain classes without annotations (classes: {n}, detections: {detections}), e.g. {names}. They are not part of these scores; if your annotations cover every species present, these detections are false positives.
eval-tab-precision-checkbox-info: The share of detections that are correct.
eval-tab-recall-checkbox-info: The share of annotated windows that are detected.
eval-tab-recording-duration-textbox-info: Leave empty to take each recording's length from the duration column, or else from its last annotation or prediction. A value applies to every recording.
eval-tab-results-header:
**Recordings:** {recordings} · **windows:** {windows} of {window} s · **classes:** {classes} · **confidence threshold:** {threshold}

A window counts as a correct detection when it overlaps an annotation of the class and the class was predicted in it.
eval-tab-sample-duration-number-info: Recordings are cut into windows of this length, and each window is scored once per class. Use the segment length of the model: 3 s for BirdNET, 5 s for Perch.
eval-tab-score-unannotated-checkbox-info: Recordings with predictions but no annotation table are scored as if they had no calls, so every prediction on them counts as a false positive. By default, they are not scored.
eval-tab-score-unannotated-checkbox-labe: Score recordings without annotation table as empty
eval-tab-select-classes-checkboxgroup-in: The annotated classes are selected by default; with none selected, they are evaluated.
eval-tab-select-recordings-checkboxgroup: With none selected, all recordings are evaluated.
eval-tab-status-annotation-only: Annotations only, so all their annotations count as missed: {names}
eval-tab-status-classes-all: ✅ Annotated classes found in the predictions (column "{column}"): all {n}
eval-tab-status-classes-some: ⚠️ Annotated classes found in the predictions (column "{column}"): {found} of {n}. Not found: {names}
eval-tab-status-column-switched: ℹ️ The prediction class column was set to "{column}", which holds the most annotated classes.
eval-tab-status-empty-annotations: ℹ️ Annotation tables without rows, counted as recordings without calls: {n}
eval-tab-status-no-annotation-tables: **Annotations** · no tables (.txt or .csv) found in this directory or its subdirectories.
eval-tab-status-no-prediction-tables: **Predictions** · no tables (.txt or .csv) found in this directory or its subdirectories.
eval-tab-status-pairing-rule: Tables are paired by recording name: the file name without its extension and without BirdNET or Raven suffixes (site1.txt ↔ site1.BirdNET.selection.table.txt), or the Recording column if one is selected.
eval-tab-status-prediction-only-empty: Predictions only, scored as recordings without calls: {names}
eval-tab-status-recordings-all: ✅ Recordings with annotations and predictions: all {n}
eval-tab-status-recordings-some: ⚠️ Recordings with annotations and predictions: {matched} of {total}
eval-tab-status-skipped-annotation: ℹ️ Skipped files in the annotation directory without the selected columns ({n}): {names}
eval-tab-status-skipped-prediction: ℹ️ Skipped files in the prediction directory without the selected columns ({n}): {names}
eval-tab-status-suggestions: 💡 Probably the same classes under other names, detected in the annotated windows: {pairs}
eval-tab-status-superseded: ℹ️ Ignored other BirdNET outputs next to the per-recording tables ({n}): {names}
eval-tab-status-window-differs: ⚠️ The window length ({window} s) differs from the segment length of the analysis ({segment} s).
eval-tab-threshold-number-info: Predictions with at least this confidence count as detections. AUROC and AP do not depend on it.
inference-settings-audio-speed-slider-in: Negative values slow down, positive values speed up. Note that audio speed modification should also be used during training in order to be effective here.
inference-settings-confidence-slider-inf: Adjust the threshold to ignore results with confidence below this level.
inference-settings-fmax-number-info: Note that frequency cut-offs should also be used during training in order to be effective here.
inference-settings-fmin-number-info: Note that frequency cut-offs should also be used during training in order to be effective here.
inference-settings-merge-consecutive-sli: Number of consecutive detections that are merged for each species. Combines N consecutive detections into one.
inference-settings-overlap-slider-info: BirdNET uses 3s segments. Determines the overlap with previous segment.
inference-settings-sensitivity-slider-in: Adjust the distribution of prediction scores. Higher values result in higher scores.
inference-settings-use-top-n-checkbox-in: Picks the top N species sorted by confidence score.
model-dir-busy-error: The model directory cannot be changed while an analysis, training or another task that uses a model is running.
model-dir-fallback-warning: The configured model directory {path} is unavailable; the default is used for this session.
model-dir-invalid-error: The selected directory cannot be created or written to.
model-dir-low-space-warning: Less than 2 GB of free space: a first model download may not fit.
model-dir-readonly-warning: The directory is read-only: the models already in it can be used, but no new models can be downloaded.
model-selection-classifier-unreadable-wa: {file} cannot be used as a classifier: {error}
model-selection-labels-mismatch-warning: The label file has {labels} entries, but the classifier outputs {classes} classes. Check that {file} belongs to this classifier.
multi-tab-additional-columns-checkbox-in: Adds additional columns to the output. "Start (s)", "End (s)", "Scientific name", "Common name", "Confidence", "File" are already included.
multi-tab-info-text:
Select the directory that contains your audio files by clicking on "Select input directory (recursive)". The analyzer will find all audio files within, even if they are contained within subdirectories.

The analysis will create result files, if you don't specify an output directory, they will be placed inside your input directory.

Thresholding and audio options can be adjusted in the inference settings.

To filter by species you can use custom species lists in the species selection section or generate a species list with given coordinates.

If you have already trained a custom classifier or do not want to use BirdNET (the default) you can select another model in the model selection section. There are translated labels for the birdnet models, which will be applied to the result files.

You can decide on the output formats you need in the output settings. All results are combined in one result file by default. To separate them by audio file, check the split option.
multi-tab-output-radio-info: Specify the output format of classifications.
multi-tab-output-textbox-placeholder: If not selected, the input directory will be used
multi-tab-resume-status-text: {completed} of {total} files have already been analyzed — the analysis will continue where it stopped.
multi-tab-split-table-checkbox-info: When enabled, a separate result table is created for each input file. Otherwise, all results are combined into a single table.
presets-invalid-analyze-params-file-erro: The selected file is not a valid analysis parameters file.
presets-invalid-name-error: Please enter a valid preset name.
presets-invalid-train-params-file-error: The selected file is not a valid training parameters file.
presets-load-analyze-params-button-label: Load settings from an analysis parameters file (birdnet.analyze-params.csv)
presets-load-train-params-button-label: Load settings from a training parameters file (*.birdnet.train-params.csv)
presets-missing-preset-error: The preset could not be read.
presets-save-failed-error: The preset could not be saved.
presets-skipped-values-warning: Some values could not be applied and were left unchanged:
review-tab-info-text:
Review and validate audio clips one species at a time, for example the segments produced by the Segments tab. The input does not have to be extracted segments, any directory of audio files works.

Select a directory, then step through the clips and mark each one as positive or negative. Marked files are moved into corresponding subfolders.

Use the history and the logistic regression plot to keep track of your progress and to determine species specific confidence thresholds.
segments-tab-collection-mode-info: Determines how segments are selected from the result files.
segments-tab-info-text:
Extract short audio segments from your recordings based on the results of a batch analysis, so you can validate detections or collect training data.

Select the folder with the original audio, the folder that contains the analysis result files, and an output folder for the extracted segments.

Set the confidence range and the number of segments to collect per species, then start the extraction. The resulting segments can be checked in the Review tab.
segments-tab-max-confidence-slider-info: Select only segments with a confidence below this threshold.
segments-tab-max-seq-number-info: Maximum number of randomly extracted segments per species.
segments-tab-min-confidence-slider-info: Select only segments with a confidence above this threshold.
segments-tab-n-bins-info: Sets the number of confidence bins for the balanced collection mode.
segments-tab-output-selection-textbox-pl: Same as audio directory if not selected
segments-tab-results-input-textbox-place: Same as audio directory if not selected
segments-tab-seq-length-number-info: Length of the extracted segments in seconds.
settings-tab-language-dropdown-info: Changes will only take effect after restarting the application.
settings-tab-model-dir-env-info: Set by the BIRDNET_APP_DATA environment variable and cannot be changed here.
settings-tab-model-dir-info: Where model files are downloaded and stored. Models that were already downloaded have to be moved or removed by hand.
settings-tab-model-dir-saved-info: Model directory saved and now in use.
settings-tab-reset-button-label: Reset all settings to default values
settings-tab-reset-info: All settings have been reset to their default values.
settings-tab-spectrogram-colormap-info: The colors used to draw spectrograms.
settings-tab-spectrogram-dynamic-range-i: Signal range shown, from the loudest level down. Lower values increase contrast, higher values reveal quieter sounds.
settings-tab-spectrogram-fft-size-info: Number of samples per FFT window. Larger windows show more frequency detail, smaller windows more time detail.
settings-tab-spectrogram-freq-scale-info: Scale of the frequency axis. Logarithmic gives low frequencies more space.
settings-tab-spectrogram-info: These settings apply to all spectrograms shown in the app. Changes take effect the next time a spectrogram is drawn.
settings-tab-spectrogram-overlap-info: Overlap between adjacent FFT windows. Higher values give a smoother image but take longer to draw.
settings-tab-theme-dropdown-info: WARNING: Changing the theme will reload the window.
single-tab-info-text:
Use this tab to explore your data and to figure out suitable settings on a few samples before running a large batch analysis in the Batch analysis tab.

Click "Select Audio File" to choose a single audio file. Enable the spectrogram option if you want to inspect the recording visually.

Thresholding, audio and species options can be adjusted in the inference settings. To use a custom classifier or a model other than BirdNET (the default), select it in the model selection section.

Press Analyze to run the model on the file. The detections appear in the table below, where you can play back each segment and download the results as a Raven table, CSV or Kaleidoscope file.
single-tab-results-truncated-warning: Showing the {shown} highest-scoring of {total} detections. Use the download buttons for the complete results.
single-tab-spectrogram-checkbox-info: Potentially slow for long audio files.
species-list-coordinates-threshold-slide: Minimum occurrence probability for a species to be included.
species-list-coordinates-week-slider-inf: Specify the week of the year the recording was made, using a simplified system where each month is divided into four weeks. Choose a value from 1 to 48.
species-list-custom-classifier-invalid-w: The selected classifier cannot be used: {0}
species-list-custom-classifier-no-labelf: No label file found in the format <customclassifier>_Labels.txt.
species-list-location-unmatched-warning: None of the selected model's species are expected at this location, so the results are not filtered by species.
species-list-radio-info: Filter species that are included in output.
species-list-unmatched-warning: {count} species in this list are not in the selected model and will be skipped.
species-tab-filename-textbox-label: Name of the file, if not specified 'species_list.txt' will be used.
species-tab-info-text:
Generate a species list for a given location that you can use to restrict the species considered in the Single analysis and Batch analysis tabs.

Choose where to save the list, then set the coordinates and the seasonal (week) filter. The frequency threshold controls how likely a species has to be at that location and time to be included.

Export the list to a text file that you can later load in the species selection of the analysis tabs.
startup-classifier-missing-warning: The custom classifier from the last session was not found; {model} is selected instead.
startup-species-list-missing-warning: The custom species list from the last session was not found; all species are used instead.
training-tab-audio-speed-slider-info: Negative values slow down, positive values speed up. -10 equals 10x decrease, 10 equals 10x increase. 1.0 equals no change.
training-tab-autotune-checkbox-info: Searches for the best hyperparameters, but takes more time.
training-tab-autotune-folds-number-info: Number of folds for cross-validation during hyperparameter tuning.
training-tab-autotune-repeats-number-inf: Number of times each trial is repeated during hyperparameter tuning (reduces variance).
training-tab-autotune-trials-number-info: Number of training runs for hyperparameter tuning.
training-tab-base-model-radio-info: BirdNET version the classifier is trained on. Its embeddings are the classifier's input, so the classifier only works with this version. When loading a cache file, the version it was created with is used.
training-tab-batchsize-number-info: Number of samples to process in a batch.
training-tab-cache-file-name-textbox-inf: The name of the cache file.
training-tab-cache-mode-radio-info: Adjust how to cache training data. Select 'none' for no caching, 'load' to load from file, and 'save' to save the compressed training data.
training-tab-classifier-textbox-info: The name of the new classifier.
training-tab-crop-mode-radio-info: Adjust how to crop samples that are longer than the model input.
training-tab-crop-overlap-number-info: Adjust the overlap of training samples.
training-tab-dropout-number-info: Higher values may help prevent overfitting.
training-tab-early-stoppage-msg: Stopped early - validation metric not improving.
training-tab-focal-loss-alpha-slider-inf: Balancing parameter. Controls weight between positive and negative examples (recommended value 0.25).
training-tab-focal-loss-gamma-slider-inf: Focusing parameter. Higher values give more weight to hard examples (recommended value 2.0).
training-tab-hiddenunits-number-info: Number of hidden units. If set to >0, a two-layer classifier is used.
training-tab-info-text:
Train your own classifier from a labeled dataset, where each subfolder of the training directory holds the audio samples of one class. If you don't have enough examples yet, you can use the Search tab to find similar calls of your target species first.

Select the training data folder and choose where the trained classifier should be saved. You can optionally provide a separate test dataset and adjust the preprocessing and training hyperparameters.

Start the training and inspect the resulting metrics. The trained classifier can afterwards be selected in the Single analysis and Batch analysis tabs.
training-tab-model-save-mode-radio-info: 'replace' will overwrite the original classification layer, leaving only the trained classes, and 'append' will combine the original classification layer with the new one.
training-tab-save-detached-classifier-ch: Saves the classifier head as detached model to reduce size
training-tab-threads-number-info: Number of parallel CPU threads used to load and decode the training audio. More threads can speed up data loading but use more CPU and memory. Ignored when training from a cache file.
training-tab-upsampling-radio-info: Balance train data by upsampling minority classes.
training-tab-upsampling-ratio-slider-inf: The minimum ratio for a minority class compared to the majority class after upsampling.
training-tab-use-focal-loss-checkbox-inf: Uses focal loss during training. This gives more weight to hard examples and helps handle class imbalance.
training-tab-use-labelsmoothing-checkbox: Applies label smoothing during training. This can help improve model generalization by preventing the model from becoming too confident.
training-tab-use-mixup-checkbox-info: Applies mixup augmentation during training. This can help improve model generalization by creating new training samples through linear interpolation.
training-tab-warning-detached-classifier: Append mode will not apply to the detached classifier.
validation-max-confidence-lower-than-min: Maximum confidence must be greater than minimum confidence
validation-no-audio-files-in-training-fo: The following training data folders do not contain any supported audio files: {0}
validation-no-directory-for-classifier-s: Please select a directory for the classifier.
validation-no-negative-samples-in-binary: Negative labels can't be used with binary classification
validation-no-valid-batch-size: Please enter a valid batch size.
validation-no-valid-cache-file-name: Please enter a valid name for the cache file.
validation-no-valid-classifier-name: Please enter a valid name for the classifier.
validation-no-valid-epoch-number: Please enter a valid number of epochs.
validation-no-valid-frequency: Please enter a valid frequency in
validation-no-valid-learning-rate: Please enter a valid learning rate.
validation-non-event-samples-required-in: Non-event samples are required for binary classification
validation-only-repeat-upsampling-for-mu: Only repeat-upsampling is available for multi-label training
